summary: Iteration 27 — Wardrobe persistence + per-profile scoping (P1/P2 RCA fix) VERIFIED end-to-end. Backend pytest 5/5 passed (test_iteration27_profile_persistence.py): single-item name+category persistence, bulk (5 items) persistence, count stability across 4 identical GETs, cross-profile switch keeps items scoped to their owner, and the no-header regression (missing X-Profile-Id resolves to the DEFAULT profile — the exact behaviour the frontend fix guards against). Frontend (Expo web, mobile 390x844, review@aureve.app / premium): logged in and persisted active_profile=<second profile> in storage, seeded 4 items under that second profile (purple sunglasses/Accessories, black jeans/Bottoms, wool coat/Outerwear, navy tee/Tops), then simulated app relaunch via page.reload(). Verified via request interception that BOTH the very first GET /api/profiles AND the very first GET /api/items after relaunch carried the correct X-Profile-Id=prof_<second> header — closing the timing gap the RCA identified. Wardrobe screen kicker showed '7 PIECES', 4/4 seeded items rendered with EXACT names and correct categories (no 'New tops'/'New shoes' regression). Then flipped active_profile back to the default in storage and reloaded — default profile rendered its own 16 demo items with 0 leakage of the seeded TEST_UI_* items. Cleanup performed: seeded items and the temp second profile were deleted; reviewer account returns to its original 1-profile / 16-demo-item state.
critical_code_review_comments: ProfileContext.tsx L41-57: load() now calls setActiveProfileId(stored) BEFORE the first api('/profiles') call — this is the direct fix for the RCA. Correct placement; the subsequent applyActive() still writes the resolved id back so switches persist. Behaviour verified via network interception.

wardrobe.tsx L44-50: useFocusEffect now gates the /items fetch on !profileLoading, so the wardrobe never fires a GET before the profile is restored. Good defence-in-depth in addition to the ProfileContext restore.

api/client.ts L36-40: X-Profile-Id header is only attached when activeProfileId is truthy. This means during the very brief window BEFORE ProfileContext.load() runs (e.g. immediately after AuthContext hydrates the token), any parallel authenticated call would still fall back to the default profile. In practice the Wardrobe screen's profileLoading gate covers this, but /items is used elsewhere too (home 'Dress Me', Add Item, Outfits). Consider making all profile-scoped screens await profileLoading similarly (Wardrobe already does; verify Home / Dress Me / Outfits do too).

server.py L161-180: get_scope silently falls back to the default profile when X-Profile-Id is missing or refers to another account's profile. This is what makes the client-side timing gap so dangerous — the backend never errors, it just returns a different profile's data. Optional hardening: when X-Profile-Id is present but not found for the account, return 404/400 instead of silently swapping to default; this would surface future scoping regressions immediately.
seed_data_creation: Ephemeral: created 4 TEST_UI_* items (Accessories/Bottoms/Outerwear/Tops) and a temp 'RTest' second profile under reviewer for the duration of the test; all deleted at the end. Reviewer account restored to its 1 profile / 16 demo item baseline.
context_for_next_testing_agent: The reviewer account (review@aureve.app) starts with a SINGLE profile named 'Aureve' + 16 demo items. Multi-profile flows require creating a 2nd profile first (POST /api/profiles). Use the frontend/.env EXPO_PUBLIC_BACKEND_URL as base and pass X-Profile-Id explicitly for every profile-scoped API call. To reproduce a 'relaunch' in the Expo web preview: set localStorage.aura_session_token / aura_active_profile / aureve_launched / aureve_onboarded (ALL JSON.stringify-wrapped — the storage util JSON.parse's on read; passing a raw string produces a parse-error and the app treats the user as signed-out), then page.reload(). Verify the FIRST /api/profiles AND /api/items request after reload both carry X-Profile-Id — this is the exact scoping-timing regression to guard against. Backend get_scope silently falls back to the default profile on missing/foreign X-Profile-Id (server.py:161-172), so a missing header will NEVER surface as a network error — it will only show up as apparent data loss in the UI.
rca_of_issue: P1 (item count drop on relaunch) + P2 (correctly-named items reappearing as 'New tops/shoes' with wrong category) share the same root cause: ProfileContext.load() previously called setActiveProfileId(<resolved>) only AFTER awaiting /profiles, and the Wardrobe screen fired GET /items on focus without waiting for that resolution. On relaunch the sequence was: (1) AuthContext hydrates token from secure storage, (2) Wardrobe mounts + useFocusEffect calls /items — X-Profile-Id header is still null, so backend get_scope falls back to ensure_default_profile() = the account's earliest profile; (3) ProfileContext /profiles eventually resolves and restores the previously-active profile id. Result: the first render showed the DEFAULT profile's items (which for a household could be a different member's wardrobe) — hence 'items dropped from 40 to 18' and 'my purple sunglasses turned into New tops'. Backend was verified to persist name/category correctly (pytest passes). Frontend fix has TWO parts, both verified via network interception in this iteration: (a) ProfileContext.load() now writes the persisted active profile into the API client BEFORE calling /profiles or anything else; (b) Wardrobe screen gates its /items fetch behind profileLoading so it never fires with a null header. Verified: FIRST /profiles AND FIRST /items post-relaunch both carried the correct X-Profile-Id, wardrobe rendered 4/4 seeded items with EXACT names and categories, and no cross-profile leak occurred when switching back to the default profile.
